name: What is the difference between a tiny home on wheels and a permanent foundation tiny home for rental?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tiny home on wheels and a permanent foundation tiny home for rental?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference lies in their classification and permanence. A tiny home on wheels (THOW) is often considered a recreational vehicle (RV) and may face different zoning restrictions, often limiting its use for long-term rentals in residential areas. A permanent foundation tiny home, however, is built directly on-site and is typically classified as an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU). ADUs are subject to traditional building codes and are generally more widely permitted for long-term rental income, offering greater stability and value as real property.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tiny homes on wheels are often RVs with rental limitations, while permanent foundation tiny homes (ADUs) are built on-site, adhere to building codes, and are typically permitted for long-term rentals.
